# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** UnitedHealthcare / Oxford — Appeals Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Jordan Iverson
Member ID: W979574719
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-20 — Reference number POC-E6EF62D505-92473**
**Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Requesting surgeon:** Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Governing policy:** *Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)* — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-20 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve this surgery. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in the plan's hands support that.

## What the plan's own policy says, and what my records show

The plan's policy, *Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)*, begins from this position:

> "Coverage Rationale Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances ."

So the question is not whether spinal procedures can be covered — the policy says they can be. The question is whether my situation is one of those circumstances. I believe it is.

The same policy states:

> "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)."

My records document exactly that situation:

- **Duration and course:** 9 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 10 weeks, from 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02, which gave 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging (2026-06-17):** MRI of the lumbar spine showing L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Examination:** positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- **Function:** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain into my right calf.
- **Risk factors:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

In other words, I tried the conservative methods. Physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and an injection were all completed and documented, and my pain was not controlled by them. The MRI identifies a specific structural cause at a specific level, and my physical exam findings match that level.

## On the criteria the notice did not identify

The policy also says:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I recognize that submitting records does not by itself guarantee approval. My point is narrower: the records that exist do document conservative care, a structural finding on imaging, a matching neurologic deficit, and a functional limitation. If those records were reviewed and found insufficient, I would like to know specifically which requirement they did not meet.

I raise this because the policy does not spell out its full medical necessity standard in the text I have. It points elsewhere:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the:"

> "Procedures, Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar (Custom) - UHG Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

The operative criteria are therefore in InterQual, which is licensed software I cannot look up on my own. The excerpts of the policy available to me also include sentences that introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in what I received — for example, a line reading "The following procedures for the treatment of spine pain are unproven and not medically necessary due to insufficient evidence of efficacy:" — and I am not able to see what follows. I am not going to guess at thresholds the plan has not published to me, and I want to be clear that nothing in this letter should be read as quoting a requirement the plan has not stated.

One criterion that does appear in the policy text I have concerns spinal instability:

> "A loss of structural support of the spine that leads to abnormal and increased movement between vertebrae outside of normal physiological limits, measured by the difference in translational alignment between lumbar vertebrae greater than or equal to 3 mm between views, as documented by flexion-extension radiographs or comparison of a supine and upright image (NASS, 2021)."

That criterion describes instability measured on flexion-extension or supine-versus-upright imaging. What my surgeon requested is a decompression (CPT 63030), and the indication documented in my chart is nerve root compression on MRI — L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis compressing the traversing L5 nerve root — not instability. If the denial rested on this instability measurement, I ask the plan to say so directly, because that measurement addresses a different finding than the one my surgeon documented as the reason for surgery.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

I am formally requesting, in writing and free of charge, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with any internal rule, guideline, or protocol relied on in denying CPT 63030. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide the specific rule or criterion it relied on for an adverse determination. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. I cannot meaningfully respond to a medical-necessity denial without seeing the standard I am said to have failed, and I ask that this material be sent to me so that I can supplement this appeal if needed.

## What I am asking for

I ask that UnitedHealthcare / Oxford overturn the denial dated 2026-08-20 (reference POC-E6EF62D505-92473) and authorize the lumbar decompression, CPT 63030, as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with relevant expertise in spine surgery, and that I receive a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion at issue if the denial is upheld.

I understand this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-16**. I am submitting it through my member account at member.uhc.com and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can also be reached at the phone number above. If the plan prefers a different submission route, please contact me and I will resend it.

Please let me know if you need any additional records from Dr. Lindqvist's office or from my physical therapy provider. I am glad to authorize their release.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Iverson**
Member ID: W979574719
Reference number: POC-E6EF62D505-92473
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures (please check before sending):**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-20
- MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-17
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, 16 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist
- Injection record, 2026-04-02
- [Any other records I choose to include]
